det.desc: Up for sale is a beautiful, authentic piece of vintage Edwardian-era sheet music: "Japanese Fan Dance" (Caractéristique), composed by the well-known British parlor music composer Theo Bonheur (a pseudonym for Charles William Dalbey). This specific edition was published in 1906 by The Vinton Music Publishing Co. This piece is a fantastic, highly collectible example of the turn-of-the-century Japonisme movement, which swept through Western art, theater, and music following the success of productions like The Mikado and The Geisha. Minor seam tearing and frayed edges.

det.desc: This is vintage sheet music for "Blue Tango," a piano solo composed by Leroy Anderson. This specific edition was published in 1951 by Mills Music, in New York. Written in 1951, "Blue Tango" became Anderson's breakout hit. It was the first instrumental recording to sell over one million copies and reached number one on the Billboard charts, staying there for 38 weeks. It is a light orchestral/concert piece that uses a rhythm reflective of an Argentinian tango. Leroy Anderson (1908–1975) was a highly educated American composer known for his classically-trained background and clever "light" orchestral works.

det.desc: This nearly seven-year old pen and ink illustration from indie comics superstar Kurt Belcher is called "I for an Eye". It was originally commissioned as concept art for Mia Falcone in Vengeance Turns, and was used to produce the sticker that you will also receive if you win this auction. Kurt Belcher was one more person who encouraged and inspired me to continue and to finished the Vengeance Turns films by producing concept art including this very special piece.
